question: How can concrete construction become circular?

answer.answer:
Making concrete work circular begins upstream of the concrete itself: the one cited route into circular construction/DfDisAssembly (VA15) runs from traceable, linked component data (VA9), on the argument that component data and material passports are what make recovery and reuse worth doing economically. The design move that follows is jointing: monolithic and glued connections are what destroy salvage value in cast concrete, and reversible connections are what preserve it, with material and energy saving and reduced CO2 and waste (VA4) as the cited payoff. The evidence base is thin and correlational beyond that: circular construction is drawn on by only 8 of the 50 coded cases, its two cited edges by 5 and 6, and the material in front of me holds no deployed project or firm record for it, so treat modularisation (PR5), early contractor involvement (CO11) and material testing (PR10) as things seen alongside circularity rather than as demonstrated causes. Note also that retrieval widened from concrete work to the general circular enabler, so what follows is a digital-fabrication finding, not a concrete-specific one.

**The one cited path in**

VA15 "Circular construction/DfDisAssembly" is a Value, and it carries exactly one inbound and one outbound cited dependency edge, both listed in full, so this is the whole of the connected picture. Inbound, VA9 "Allow traceable/linked data" enables VA15, on the grounds that component data and material passports make recovery and reuse economically viable [1], backed by peer-reviewed evidence; that edge is carried by 5 of the 50 coded cases, while 26 of the 50 draw on VA9 [2] in its own right and 8 draw on VA15 [2]. The asymmetry matters: data traceability is common practice in the record, circularity built on it is not.

Outbound, VA15 enables VA4 "Material/energy saving/reduce CO2/waste", because glued and monolithic joints limit salvage potential while reversible connection design under design for disassembly enables material recovery [3], also peer-reviewed and carried by 6 of the 50. That sentence is the most directly concrete-relevant thing in the retrieved material, since cast-in-place work is monolithic by default. 15 of the 50 cases draw on VA4. [2]

A second use of the same data layer is worth acting on: VA9 mitigates RI3 "Increase cost/investment uncertainty", because material passports reduce uncertainty about the circular potential and economics of disassembled elements [2], carried by 7 of the 50, with 13 of the 50 drawing on RI3 [2]. So the data investment does double duty, opening the circular path and damping the investment risk that usually blocks it.

**What sits beside circularity, as correlation only**

The enablers most often co-occurring with VA15 are material testing (PR10) at weight 8, integrate supply chain (VA14) at 7, modularisation (PR5), excavation/transportation (PR16), increase cost/investment uncertainty (RI3), early contractor involvement (CO11) and DfMA for DFAB process (PR9) at 6, design engineer (AC3) and bespoke/customised design (AT1) at 5, CNC machines (RE7) and subtractive manufacturing (PR7) at 4, and increase material usage/waste (RI16) at 3 [4]. 125 enablers co-occur with VA15 in total [4], so this is a cut, not a closed list. None of these is an asserted dependency on circularity: they are statistical companions. The presence of RI3 among them, alongside the cited mitigation edge, is consistent with circular projects carrying unusual cost uncertainty.

**Concrete-specific constraints in the retrieved edges**

Two edges bear on concrete processes rather than on circularity, and they are the compliance watchpoints. PR3 "Additive manufacturing" depends on RI18 "Regulatory/legal concern", because 3D printed concrete walls require certification against acceptance criteria for structural strength, fire safety and durability [5], on standards evidence and carried by 2 of the 50. PR8 "On-site DFAB" likewise depends on RI18, with on-site 3D concrete printing proceeding through an alternative-means approval pathway [6], also standards evidence and carried by 2 of the 50. 4 of the 50 cases draw on PR3 [2] and 12 on RI18 [2]. Reversible, demountable concrete connections would face the same approval route, though the retrieved material does not assert that link.

**What the record does not support**

There is no deployed process record, census record or named firm in this context bearing on circular concrete, so nothing here rests on a built case; the whole of the circularity claim is literature. And the cited dependency layer is sparse in general: 100 edges touch 68 of the 140 enablers, leaving 72 with no cited edge, and 48% of Values have none [2], so the absence of further routes into VA15 reflects what the literature has connected, not what practice does.
